findings.title: `getBaseConditions` checks `authConditions` for truthiness, so the filter-only branch can never run
findings.description: `getAuthorizationConditions()` is typed to return `Prisma.Sql` and never `null`, so `if (authConditions && filterConditions)` reduces to `if (filterConditions)`. Because of that, the `else if (filterConditions)` branch is unreachable: when a filter exists, the first branch always runs. The output is still correct, since the auth clause is always present, but the branch is dead code and suggests a null case that the types rule out. Either drop the `authConditions` check or make the nullability explicit in the return type.

findings.title: Constructor option type is widened to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` without a visible narrowing for `this.options`
findings.description: The constructor parameter changed from `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (a discriminated union) to the flat `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, whose `scope` is a plain union. The field assignment `this.options = options` is outside the shown hunk, so I could not confirm from the diff that it still type-checks against `InsightsBookingServiceOptions | null`. Please confirm that the project's type check passes.
